dimensions.name: Employment Tenure Stability
dimensions.definition: How long each adult in the household has held their current role, taken jointly, as a proxy for income reliability and risk of near-term employment disruption.
dimensions.high_end: Both adults have long, unbroken employment histories with their current employers, signalling strong income continuity.
dimensions.low_end: One or both adults began their current role recently, leaving income tenure short and less proven.

dimensions.name: Household Income Cushion
dimensions.definition: The household's total gross income relative to the assumed minimum needed to carry co-op housing costs, measuring how much financial headroom exists.
dimensions.high_end: Household income is well above the housing-cost floor, providing a large cushion for unexpected expenses or arrears risk.
dimensions.low_end: Household income sits close to the minimum threshold, leaving little buffer for income disruption or unplanned costs.

dimensions.name: Dual-Earner Income Resilience
dimensions.definition: How evenly household income is split between both adults, measuring how much of total income survives the loss of either earner.
dimensions.high_end: Income is split roughly equally, so losing one income still leaves the household with roughly half its earnings.
dimensions.low_end: Income is heavily concentrated in one earner, so losing that earner would critically impair ability to meet housing charges.

dimensions.name: Hands-On Trades & Maintenance Skills
dimensions.definition: Whether the household holds licensed trade qualifications or demonstrated practical maintenance skills directly applicable to building upkeep.
dimensions.high_end: At least one adult holds a recognized trade licence or equivalent and explicitly offers it for building maintenance tasks.
dimensions.low_end: No trade or technical skills claimed; household self-describes as unable to perform physical building repairs.

dimensions.name: Administrative & Governance Skills
dimensions.definition: The household's demonstrated competence in co-op administrative functions — scheduling, minutes, correspondence, meeting facilitation — based on stated roles and past practice.
dimensions.high_end: Adults have concretely practiced core administrative co-op functions (running meetings, writing minutes, coordinating schedules) and can describe specific past instances.
dimensions.low_end: Administrative capability is asserted but not grounded in specific past roles or examples, or not mentioned at all.

dimensions.name: Systems Documentation Discipline
dimensions.definition: The degree to which the household demonstrates a practice of writing things down, maintaining records, and ensuring institutional knowledge transfers smoothly to future volunteers or committee members.
dimensions.high_end: An adult explicitly describes writing documentation so future volunteers aren't lost, grounded in prior governance practice.
dimensions.low_end: No mention of documentation habits; skills and processes are described without reference to recording or transferring knowledge.

dimensions.name: Financial Oversight Experience
dimensions.definition: The household's demonstrated history of managing or scrutinizing budgets, financial reporting, or fiscal accountability in an organizational or committee setting.
dimensions.high_end: An adult has directly managed or reviewed organizational budgets in a governance role and explicitly offers budget transparency and financial oversight to the co-op.
dimensions.low_end: No financial oversight experience mentioned; offers to contribute financially are absent or stated without supporting experience.

dimensions.name: Social-Service Navigation Skill
dimensions.definition: Whether the household can professionally connect neighbours with external city services, benefits, or social support systems — a soft-infrastructure contribution distinct from trades or governance.
dimensions.high_end: An adult works in a relevant field (e.g., social work, community development) and explicitly offers to help residents access city services and benefits they may not know they qualify for.
dimensions.low_end: No professional background or stated capacity in social services, resident advocacy, or external resource navigation.

dimensions.name: Co-op Governance Experience
dimensions.definition: How much direct, substantive experience the household has with co-operative or collective housing governance structures — committees, work-hour systems, shared decision-making.
dimensions.high_end: Grew up inside a housing co-op and/or held active roles in co-op governance (committees, work scheduling, member decisions) with fluent understanding of how co-ops actually function.
dimensions.low_end: No prior housing co-op experience; closest analogue is strata or similar body, or experience is entirely abstract or second-hand.

dimensions.name: Work-Shift & Unglamorous-Task Commitment
dimensions.definition: How explicitly and credibly the household commits to fulfilling unglamorous, recurring co-op labour obligations — cleaning, sorting, maintenance days — based on stated intent and demonstrated prior behaviour.
dimensions.high_end: Household explicitly volunteers for the least-desirable tasks, names specific jobs they will take on, and frames reliability and follow-through as core personal values backed by prior behaviour.
dimensions.low_end: Willingness to do required labour is not specifically stated, implied only generically, or entirely absent.

dimensions.name: Emergency / On-Call Availability
dimensions.definition: Whether the household explicitly offers to be available for unscheduled small emergencies or on-call maintenance needs in the building.
dimensions.high_end: Household explicitly states both adults are comfortable being on the on-call list for small emergencies.
dimensions.low_end: Household does not mention on-call or emergency availability; contribution framing is entirely scheduled or planned.

dimensions.name: Co-op Philosophy Articulation
dimensions.definition: How clearly and substantively the household articulates a personal understanding of cooperative living as a value system, beyond just describing practical contributions.
dimensions.high_end: Essay articulates a coherent co-op philosophy (mutual aid, shared responsibility, collective problem-solving) grounded in lived values and specific reasoning.
dimensions.low_end: Motivation for co-op living is thin or instrumental; no developed account of why the co-op model matters to the household.

dimensions.name: Community-Building Proactivity
dimensions.definition: The degree to which the household actively initiates social infrastructure within the co-op — events, clubs, welcome programs, kids activities — rather than simply participating in what already exists.
dimensions.high_end: Household describes running or founding community activities (book clubs, new-member welcome events, kids programming) with no prompt, framing initiation as a core contribution.
dimensions.low_end: Household does not describe initiating community activities; contributions are reactive (showing up, being available) rather than proactive social creation.

dimensions.name: Social Integration Orientation
dimensions.definition: The degree to which the household frames its motivation in terms of building personal social relationships and belonging among neighbours — beyond fulfilling functional obligations.
dimensions.high_end: Household describes concrete social practices (book clubs, baking for neighbours, knowing people on the street) and explicitly articulates wanting to be embedded in a community of neighbours.
dimensions.low_end: Motivation is framed primarily in functional or values-based terms without emphasis on personal social relationship-building.

dimensions.name: External Community Involvement
dimensions.definition: The household's active participation in community organisations or activities outside the co-op, reflecting a broader pattern of civic engagement.
dimensions.high_end: Adults are actively involved in named external community organisations and take organising or leadership roles within them.
dimensions.low_end: No external community involvement mentioned; civic engagement is framed only in the context of the co-op itself.

dimensions.name: Existing Ties to This Co-op
dimensions.definition: Whether the household has pre-existing personal connections to current members of this specific co-op, which may ease integration and signal informed motivation.
dimensions.high_end: Household has a close personal relationship with a current member of this specific co-op who actively informed their decision to apply.
dimensions.low_end: No stated personal connection to any current member; knowledge of the community is entirely external.

dimensions.name: Environmental Stewardship Practice
dimensions.definition: The degree to which the household demonstrates concrete, habitual environmental stewardship behaviours in their personal lives, beyond general stated values.
dimensions.high_end: Household describes specific, habitual eco-conscious practices (e.g., packing out trash on outdoor trips, low-waste habits) integrated into daily or recreational life, volunteered without prompting.
dimensions.low_end: No environmental practices mentioned, or reference is only to compliance with standard co-op recycling duties.

dimensions.name: Children's Program Coordination Capacity
dimensions.definition: The household's demonstrated ability and stated willingness to organise and run children's or family-focused programming during co-op work weekends or community events.
dimensions.high_end: An adult explicitly offers to coordinate kids' programs during work events and has relevant professional experience (e.g., teaching, childcare coordination) supporting that offer.
dimensions.low_end: No offer or capacity for children's programming mentioned; household does not connect their skills to family-community activities.

dimensions.name: New-Member Orientation & Integration Role
dimensions.definition: Whether the household explicitly offers to run or support new-member onboarding, orientation, and welcome processes.
dimensions.high_end: An adult has concretely run new-member orientation programs in a co-op or similar setting with specific practices described, and explicitly offers to continue this role.
dimensions.low_end: Willingness to welcome members is mentioned only in passing or not at all, without supporting experience.

dimensions.name: Mentorship & Peer Support Orientation
dimensions.definition: The degree to which the household explicitly frames its co-op contribution in terms of mentoring newer members, sharing knowledge, and supporting peers through difficulty.
dimensions.high_end: An adult explicitly offers to mentor new members, share institutional knowledge, and support peers, framing this as a primary contribution.
dimensions.low_end: No mention of mentorship or peer-support roles; contributions are framed in task-completion or administrative terms.

dimensions.name: Household Size as Long-Term Stability Anchor
dimensions.definition: The number of household members as a signal of how invested the family is in long-term stable housing — larger families with school-age children typically have stronger incentives to remain.
dimensions.high_end: Large household with multiple school-age children, creating strong roots and high relocation cost — powerful reasons to remain a stable, long-term member.
dimensions.low_end: Smaller household with one young child or no children, leaving more flexibility to exit — fewer structural anchors to long-term tenancy.

dimensions.name: Household Size & Space Demand
dimensions.definition: The total number of people in the household, bearing on unit size requirements, demand on shared amenities, and the household's footprint within the co-op.
dimensions.high_end: Smaller household placing lower demands on unit size, shared spaces, and common facilities.
dimensions.low_end: Larger household requiring more space and generating higher usage of shared infrastructure and common areas.

dimensions.name: Application Essay Engagement Depth
dimensions.definition: The thoroughness and specificity with which the household engages with application prompts — whether answers are detailed and prompt-specific or brief and generic.
dimensions.high_end: Every prompt receives a substantive, specific answer drawing on personal experience, named examples, and tailored reasoning for this co-op.
dimensions.low_end: Most prompts receive only one or two generic sentences without named examples, specific practices, or tailored reasoning.

dimensions.name: Pet Complexity & Co-habitation Considerations
dimensions.definition: The number and type of pets the household keeps, relevant to co-op rules, neighbour comfort, shared space use, and inter-pet compatibility with other residents.
dimensions.high_end: No pets or a single low-impact pet, minimising friction with co-op pet policies and neighbour sensitivities.
dimensions.low_end: Multiple pets of mixed types (e.g., both a dog and a cat), requiring more accommodation and potentially creating neighbour-interaction or policy challenges.

settled.name: Employment Tenure Stability
settled.decision: Both axes measure the same thing — length of current employment as a proxy for income reliability — using the same direction (longer = more stable = higher fit). An applicant with long joint tenure scores high on both. Merged.

settled.name: Household Income Cushion
settled.decision: Both axes measure total household income as a financial buffer against co-op costs — same applicant ranks the same on both, and higher income is the desirable end for both. Merged.

settled.name: Dual-Earner Income Resilience
settled.decision: Both axes measure income distribution between earners as resilience to job loss — identical concept, identical direction. An applicant with a balanced split scores high on both. Merged.

settled.name: Hands-On Trades & Maintenance Skills
settled.decision: Both axes measure possession of licensed or demonstrable trade/technical skills for building maintenance. Same applicant scores the same on both; more skill = higher fit in both. Merged.

settled.name: Administrative & Governance Skills
settled.decision: Both axes measure the same general administrative and meeting-management competence in a co-op governance context, with more demonstrated competence as the desirable end. Financial oversight and documentation discipline are carved out separately in R1 and kept distinct (see those axes). Merged only the core admin/organizational overlap here.

settled.name: Systems Documentation Discipline
settled.decision: Kept distinct from general administrative skills: a person can run excellent meetings yet never document for successors, so a plausible applicant can score high on admin skills and low here. Single source key, kept as-is.

settled.name: Financial Oversight Experience
settled.decision: Both axes measure demonstrated experience managing or scrutinizing budgets in a governance context, with hands-on financial oversight as the desirable end. An applicant who has reviewed co-op financial statements and volunteered to keep numbers honest scores high on both. Merged.

settled.name: Social-Service Navigation Skill
settled.decision: Both axes describe the same competency: a professional background enabling residents to navigate external services and benefits. Same applicant (e.g., a social worker who volunteers this role) scores high on both. Merged.

settled.name: Co-op Governance Experience
settled.decision: Both axes measure direct housing co-op governance experience, with more hands-on co-op-specific experience as the desirable end. An applicant who served on a co-op membership committee scores high on both. Merged.

settled.name: Work-Shift & Unglamorous-Task Commitment
settled.decision: Both axes measure the same thing — enthusiasm and credible commitment to unglamorous, recurring co-op labour — with explicit, specific, behaviour-backed commitment as the desirable end. Same applicant scores alike on both. Merged.

settled.name: Emergency / On-Call Availability
settled.decision: Kept distinct from work-shift commitment: scheduled labour and unscheduled on-call availability are different obligations. A plausible applicant eagerly signs up for work weekends yet explicitly declines an on-call list (or vice versa). Single source key, kept as-is.

settled.name: Co-op Philosophy Articulation
settled.decision: Distinct from essay engagement depth (which measures thoroughness of answering prompts) and social integration orientation (which measures relationship-building motivation). An applicant can write a brief but philosophically rich statement or a lengthy application with no articulated values. Kept as-is.

settled.name: Community-Building Proactivity
settled.decision: Kept distinct from social integration orientation (which is about wanting to form personal relationships) and external community involvement (which is about outside civic engagement). An applicant can be a keen event organiser inside the co-op yet be socially reserved in personal relationship-building, or heavily involved outside but not a self-starter inside. Kept as-is.

settled.name: Social Integration Orientation
settled.decision: Kept distinct from community-building proactivity (initiating infrastructure for others) and co-op philosophy articulation (articulating values). A person can deeply value personal neighbourhood relationships yet never organise an event. Single source key, kept as-is.

settled.name: External Community Involvement
settled.decision: Kept distinct from community-building proactivity (which is internal to the co-op) and social integration orientation (personal relationships). An applicant can be heavily externally civically engaged yet never initiate anything inside the co-op. Single source key, kept as-is.

settled.name: Existing Ties to This Co-op
settled.decision: Both axes measure the same thing — a pre-existing personal relationship with a current member of this specific co-op. Same applicant scores identically on both; having that relationship is the desirable end for both. Merged.

settled.name: Environmental Stewardship Practice
settled.decision: Both axes measure the same concept — demonstrated environmental behaviours as a lifestyle practice — with concrete habitual action as the desirable end. The R0 label 'ethos' and R1 label 'practice' describe the same measurement. Merged.

settled.name: Children's Program Coordination Capacity
settled.decision: Both axes measure whether the household proposes and has capacity to run children's programming for the co-op community. Same applicant scores alike; explicit offer backed by relevant experience is the desirable end. Merged.

settled.name: New-Member Orientation & Integration Role
settled.decision: Both axes measure the same capacity and willingness to run new-member orientation and onboarding. Same applicant scores alike on both. Merged.

settled.name: Mentorship & Peer Support Orientation
settled.decision: Kept distinct from new-member orientation role (which is about structured onboarding processes) and community-building proactivity (which is about initiating events). Mentorship is a sustained relational investment in an individual, not a programme or event. Single source key, kept as-is.

settled.name: Household Size as Long-Term Stability Anchor
settled.decision: Kept distinct from household_size_and_space_demand (R1), which has the OPPOSITE desirable end (smaller = higher fit due to lower space demands). Merging would flip one axis's direction and lose a committee distinction. Kept as-is with its own desirable end (larger = more anchored).

source_names.household_size_long_term_anchor: Household Size as Long-Term Stability Anchor

settled.name: Household Size & Space Demand
settled.decision: Kept distinct from household_size_long_term_anchor (R0), which has the OPPOSITE desirable end (larger = more stable). The same underlying fact (household size) generates two legitimately opposing fit stories; both are kept so the committee can decide which matters more for their context.

settled.name: Children's School-Age Community Engagement Potential
settled.decision: Kept distinct from child-inclusive contribution capacity (which is about what the household's adults do for children's programming) and from household-size axes (which measure space demands or stability). This axis measures what the children themselves bring to community vitality. Single source key, kept as-is.

settled.name: Application Essay Engagement Depth
settled.decision: Kept distinct from co-op philosophy articulation (depth of values statement) and from all skills axes. Essay engagement measures application effort and specificity as a process signal, regardless of content domain. Single source key, kept as-is.

settled.name: Pet Complexity & Co-habitation Considerations
settled.decision: No counterpart in R0. Kept as-is — a household with multiple mixed pets is a meaningfully different co-habitation consideration from one with no pets, and this is not captured by any other axis. Single source key, kept as-is.
